subject: Acme AI inference evaluation — recap, competitive notes & next tests
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Acme AI inference evaluation — brief recap & next steps

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same page:

Summary (what we heard)
- Primary goal: drop p95 latency for 1–2k token responses while keeping cost predictable for API-driven inference.
- Comparison focus: your current hyperscaler endpoints (v2) vs Redwood hosted/dedicated variants for latency, p99, and tokens/sec at target concurrency.

Key Redwood differentiators we highlighted (brief)
- Prefix/KV caching and warm-up controls to reduce repeated KV miss penalties.
- Continuous batching and fine-grained processor selection → better tokens/sec at moderate concurrency.
- Built-in fallback model routing to preserve availability when capacity is constrained.

Proposed A/B test (high level)
- Compare Hyperscaler-v2 vs Redwood-hosted and Redwood-dedicated (same model family, quantized where applicable).
- Test dataset: 2k sample requests representative of your typical prompt distribution (we'll use the sample you shared).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and median cost per 1k tokens.
- Target runs: 10k requests per test, concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16.
- Special: include cold-start exercise (scale-to-zero then burst) to capture p95 cold tail.

Next steps / asks
1) Can you confirm the dataset location and whether we can run tests from your eu-west (if you prefer region testing) or from our us-east/gcp region?
2) I'll attach a very short bench summary from our demo and a suggested runbook; Marissa and Connor will add config details.
3) Proposed windows: Wed 11/24 morning or Thu 11/25 afternoon (your timezone).

Attachments: 20261120-acme-quick-bench-summary.pdf

If that looks right, we'll draft a detailed runbook and schedule.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake

Thanks Jordan — good summary. A few clarifying Qs before we lock dates:

1) Region: we'd prefer eu-west for initial tests (our prod lives there). Can Redwood exercise both hosted eu-west and a dedicated instance in AWS eu-west?
2) Cold-starts are our primary concern — especially the p95 tail for first 30s after a scale event. Can your plan surface that metric separately (not averaged into steady-state)?
3) Bench harness: will you reuse our payloads or run synthetic variants? We want to make sure the token distribution matches conversational flows (lots of short instr + occasional long context).
4) Cost: can you provide a rough 1M-token estimate for Redwood-hosted vs your dedicated pricing to compare TCO with the hyperscaler?

We can do Thu 11/25 afternoon CET if you can confirm region and runbook.

Alyssa

Alyssa — great questions, answered inline below. I've also attached a short runbook and the bench config we'll use so your infra team can eyeball it. Links at the bottom.

1) Region: yes — we can run the hosted tests in eu-west (we have regional endpoints), and we can provision a short-lived dedicated pool in AWS eu-west for a like-for-like comparison. If you prefer, we can also run a third leg from our us-east cluster to show cross-region variance.

2) Cold-starts: we'll capture cold-start windows explicitly. Plan: scale-to-zero then send a 60s burst, capture p50/p95/p99 for the first 60s and then for steady-state (60–300s). We'll label cold vs steady in the results CSV.

3) Payloads: we'll use your dataset (you mentioned a shared S3 link) as the primary source. For safety we'll run a small synthetic pass to validate harness stability but real analysis will use your data. Please confirm the S3 path or share a signed URL.

4) Cost: rough order-of-magnitude: Redwood-hosted (optimized batch + quantization) ~ $X.XX per 1M tokens; dedicated depends on committed capacity — I'll share a dedicated vs hosted TCO table in the full runbook. (I'll flag finance to provide an exact quote after we pick config.)

Proposed schedule: Thu 2026-11-25 09:00–12:00 CET (we can split benchmark legs across the window). Please confirm and we'll send calendar invites.

Adding a few engineering specifics so the benchmark produces actionable numbers (copying Alyssa so their team sees config):

Bench parameters (concrete)
- Requests: 10,000 end-to-end (your dataset), concurrency sweep: [1,4,8,16].
- Payload lengths: we will bucket by token count: short (<64), medium (64-512), long (512-2048) to report tokens/sec by bucket.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, mean tokens/sec over the steady-state window, request error rate, GPU utilization (for dedicated runs).
- Cold-start exercise: 3 cold pulses per run (scale down to zero between pulses) to capture tail behavior.

Bench config notes
- Use continuous batching + KV cache warmup (prefill top 200 prefix keys) for Redwood legs to reflect prod-like optimizations.
- For Hyperscaler-v2 legs, we'll run their best-practices config you shared and include a quantized variant if available.
- We'll provide raw CSVs and a short report with p50/p95/p99 tables and tokens/sec plots.

Infra asks for Acme
- Please open inbound rule for runner IPs (listed in runbook) and provide the S3 path or signed URL for the dataset.
- If you want the dedicated pool in your AWS account, share the account ID and a short IAM role we can assume; otherwise we can spin in our test tenancy within eu-west.

I'll be online during the Thu window and Connor will lead the dedicated provisioning. Jordan — happy to scrub the final runbook and publish the calendar invites when you confirm.

Marissa
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
